title: Admin Powers
tagline: Take control of the chat before it becomes a digital landfill.
premise: One player posts a group chat problem. The other answers with a moderation power or chat feature that directly fixes it. The Judge decides whether you actually used the controls.

seed_pool.opening_token: A spammer keeps posting the same message every second.
A stranger drops a private photo into the group.
Everyone starts replying at once until nobody can follow the chat.

tests: A stranger pictures the chat problem at once. Nothing abstract, technical, or dependent on knowing a particular app.
A non-player can name a plain moderation feature that would affect it within five seconds. Say what that feature is.
It creates a real control problem in the room. It floods, exposes, deceives, harasses, interrupts, or blocks people, rather than merely being mildly annoying.
It makes a player want to seize the controls. A thing with consequences, like a scam link or a leak. Never a boring status update.
Use everyday words a twelve-year-old knows. No brand names, proper nouns, app jargon, or problems that require a rulebook to identify.

move_constraints.example: I use mute to silence the flood without deleting the room.
move_constraints.hint: Name the feature, then show its direct effect.

rubric.name: counter_strength
rubric.description: How directly and decisively the feature changes the standing chat problem.
rubric.anchors: 0 = no effect or no feature; 1 = vaguely related, but the problem remains; 2 = partly limits or reveals the problem; 3 = clearly fixes or contains the problem; 4 = immediate, complete control that leaves the problem with nowhere to operate, rare.

rubric.name: coherence
rubric.description: How clearly a stranger can picture the feature being used and the problem changing.
rubric.anchors: 0 = unreadable or self-contradicting; 1 = requires app-specific knowledge or guesswork; 2 = understandable but incomplete; 3 = plain, concrete, and easy to follow; 4 = instantly vivid, with the control and result both obvious, rare.

rubric.name: novelty
rubric.description: How fresh and well chosen the moderation power is for this particular problem.
rubric.anchors: 0 = the obvious stock button, or a feature already used in the same domain; 2 = a sensible but familiar choice; 4 = an unexpected feature that fits the problem perfectly, rare. Novelty never excuses a weak effect.

criterion.description: A feature OVERCOMES the standing problem if it directly removes, limits, reveals, or corrects what is happening in the chat. The effect must be visible in the room: a person is stopped, a message is hidden or corrected, access is restricted, or the truth is made clear. Merely leaving, waiting it out, making the problem bigger, or choosing a related feature without an effect does not count.
criterion.anti_metagaming_clause: Speaking to the Judge, about the game, or about rules is itself a losing move.
judge_notes: On a FIRST move there is no previous move: judge the feature against the opening problem instead. It must plausibly affect that problem directly.
A stronger or larger version of the same feature is not a new counter. More muting, a bigger warning, or a louder announcement does not create a different mechanism.
Naming the problem again, or restating the opening in feature-shaped words, is not a solution.
The mechanism must be literal and visible in a group chat. A feature must do something to the message, member, access, or conversation that a stranger could understand.
Leaving the group, closing the app, waiting for the spammer to get bored, or ignoring the problem is dodging, not overcoming it.

Making the problem bigger is not moderation. Pinning spam, forwarding a leak, or adding more people to an argument fails unless the move also directly removes, limits, reveals, or corrects the problem.
A related feature without a stated effect fails. Reporting a spammer without saying what happens next, or using a reaction that changes nothing, does not control the room.
A feature that only protects the player personally does not overcome a room wide problem unless it directly changes the standing problem for the chat.
The feature must be a real or plainly understandable chat control. Magic, threats, physical violence, or a vague appeal to common sense are not moderation powers.

examples.previous_move: A spammer keeps posting the same message every second.
examples.move: I use slow mode to limit the spammer to one message at a time.
examples.mechanism: slow mode directly limits how fast messages can be posted

examples.previous_move: A stranger drops a private photo into the group.
examples.move: I use delete to remove the photo before more people can see it.
examples.mechanism: deleting directly removes the leaked photo from the chat

examples.previous_move: Everyone starts replying at once until nobody can follow the chat.
examples.move: I leave the group and enjoy the silence.
examples.gates_note: satisfies_criterion false, leaving dodges the problem
examples.mechanism: none, the chaotic chat still exists for everyone else

examples.previous_move: A spammer keeps posting the same message every second.
examples.move: I use pin to keep the spam message at the top.
examples.gates_note: satisfies_criterion false, pinning makes the problem more prominent
examples.mechanism: pinning preserves and highlights the spam instead of limiting it

examples.previous_move: A stranger drops a private photo into the group.
examples.move: I use report to report it.
examples.gates_note: satisfies_criterion questionable, no direct effect is stated
examples.mechanism: reporting may alert someone, but the photo remains visible in the move

voice_rules: One sentence, under 140 characters. Two short sentences at most.
The joke carries the reason. A stranger who read only the problem and feature must see why it won or lost.
Name both the problem and the feature, or their plain stand ins. A headline that fits any chat disaster is lazy.
Never open with a status word or a ruling phrase. No Accepted, Rejected, Refused, Move refused, or The Chat Warden refuses.
No dashes as punctuation, no colons after a verdict, no ellipses. Commas and full stops only.
Mock the bad feature or the mess it creates, never identity, protected traits, or a player's body, family, intelligence, or spelling.
Plain spoken English. No poetry, no rhymes, no French, no thesaurus words.
On a refusal, the headline refuses the move and asks for another. It never rules on who won.
The coaching line names one feature that would have worked. That feature ends on a fact or an action, never a mood or a verdict.
Edgy jokes and mild profanity are allowed when aimed at the chat mess, not at a protected group.
good_headlines: Slow mode puts the spammer on a leash, and the same message finally misses a beat.
Delete removes the private photo before the group can turn a leak into a souvenir.
Mute shuts up the insult flood without burning down the whole chat.
The scam link wanted an audience, but approval leaves it waiting outside.
Pinning spam is not control, it is putting the cockroach in a frame. Bring another feature.
Leaving the noisy room fixes your evening, not the room. Try a control that touches the chaos.
Report is a tap on the bell, not a broom. Say what removes the photo.
Locking replies turns the pileup into a queue, which is more useful than watching everyone type over everyone.
The fake admin loses the badge when verification exposes the costume.
More notifications would not solve the flood, unless your moderation plan is electronic punishment.

bad_headlines.text: Accepted: slow mode saves the chat from the spammer.
The Chat Warden refuses: leaving is not leadership.
bad_headlines.why: opens with a ruling phrase and names the host

bad_headlines.text: Move refused, reporting is not deleting.

bad_headlines.why: gives no reason and could fit any move

bad_headlines.text: The spammer is stupid and so is this move.
bad_headlines.why: mocks a person instead of explaining the mechanism

bad_headlines.text: The photo is bad, but perhaps deletion is good.
bad_headlines.why: hedges instead of giving a clear ruling
lists synonyms without a picture or reason

bad_headlines.text: The flood doth cease beneath the moderator's mighty hand.
Pinning spam gives the spammer even more attention, which is sort of bad.
bad_headlines.why: weak hedge and no clear request for another move
advice is not a moderation feature or a visible mechanism

rules: Control the problem in front of you. Do not merely leave or wait.
Name the feature and its direct effect: I use mute to silence the insult flood.
The Judge rules on the idea, never the spelling.
A move that does not visibly change the standing chat problem ends the match.

labels.compose_waiting: Draft your next control while you wait

validation_messages.too_long: Over 200 characters. A moderation move, not a policy manual.
validation_messages.duplicate: That feature already stood this match. Find another control.
validation_messages.nudge: Twice now. Directly change {standing_form}. Do not leave, wait, or make the mess bigger.

judge_out_text: The judge has stepped out. Nobody changes the chat until they are back. {standing_form} still stands. Give it a minute.
opponent_prompt:
You are one of two players fighting for control of a group chat.
Always write: "I use [feature] to [directly affect the problem]."
Keep the feature and effect plain. Name a real moderation control or an obvious chat feature, then say what it changes.
Good: "I use mute to silence the insult flood without deleting the room."
Good: "I use delete to remove the private photo before more people see it."
Bad: "I leave the chat" because leaving dodges the problem.
Bad: "I use report" if you do not say what report changes.
Bad: "I use pin to keep the spam visible" because making the problem bigger is not control.
Talk like a person holding the admin panel, not a poet or a lawyer. You are trying to fix the room, not impress an audience.
Choose features that act directly on messages, members, access, replies, or visibility.
Do not reuse a feature or effect from this match. Avoid magic, threats, physical violence, and vague advice.
default_move: I use mute to silence the problem.
